memory_update.text: KRT is the cleanest public underfollowed candidate for restaurant supplies/packaging/disposables because its business is directly tied to disposable foodservice products used by restaurants and foodservice settings.

GPK should be tracked as a mid-cap fiber/paperboard packaging candidate with explicit QSR cups, lids and food-container exposure, though restaurant exposure is diluted by broader packaging end markets.
REYN is a hypothesis-level restaurant-disposables adjacent name via Hefty Tableware; survival in later layers depends on proving meaningful commercial/catering/foodservice channel exposure.
AMCR is the public reference wrapper for former Berry Global foodservice packaging assets after the April 30, 2025 merger, but exposure purity is low relative to KRT and GPK.
Pactiv Evergreen/Novolex is a major private benchmark for this node but is no longer an investable standalone US-listed candidate after the April 1, 2025 Novolex transaction.

Next layer should verify pricing power for the node: resin/paper input cost pass-through, customer concentration, distributor dependence, import/tariff risk, sustainability regulation and whether foodservice volumes are actually growing.

node: Restaurant supplies, packaging, tableware, napkins, cups, and disposables
summary: Layer 1B expanded the public-company universe for restaurant packaging/disposables. The cleanest underfollowed direct exposure found is Karat Packaging (KRT), a small-cap manufacturer/distributor of disposable foodservice products used by restaurant chains and foodservice settings. Graphic Packaging (GPK) is a mid-cap paperboard packaging reference/underfollowed hybrid with disclosed cups, lids and food containers sold to foodservice companies and QSRs. Reynolds Consumer Products (REYN) is less directly tied to restaurants but has a Hefty Tableware disposable plates/bowls/cups/cutlery segment that may participate in catering/foodservice-adjacent demand, requiring channel verification. Amcor (AMCR), after acquiring Berry Global, is a large-cap context anchor for broad foodservice packaging scale, but its exposure is diluted across many packaging end markets. Pactiv Evergreen/Novolex is highly relevant to this node but was excluded from candidates because Pactiv Evergreen ceased to be a standalone public equity after the April 1, 2025 Novolex combination.
